h1: Room@Vipa Bangkok — A Small Boutique on Vibhavadi Soi 44 That Guests Keep Coming Back To
intro: Kaset isn't a tourist district — but if you have business in northern Bangkok or need a solid, affordable base near Kasetsart University, Room@Vipa is the name that keeps appearing in real guest reviews. Located on Vibhavadi Rangsit Soi 44 in Chatuchak, it sits ~750 m from Bang Khen SRT Red Line station — making Don Mueang Airport surprisingly accessible. 33 rooms, open since 2014. From approx. ฿550/night. Score 8.7/10 from 89 Trip.com reviews, with location scoring highest at 9.2.

body.html: A guesthouse that earns its repeat visitors — Room@Vipa has been welcoming guests since 2014 on Vibhavadi Rangsit Soi 44, Lat Yao sub-district, Chatuchak district. The name comes from the Vibhavadi road it sits on. At 33 rooms, this is genuinely boutique-scale — not a sprawling hotel chain where guests feel anonymous. What makes it stand out is what the data shows: multiple TripAdvisor reviews are from guests who have returned 10–15 times, describing a "cosy and homely vibe" and staff who remember their faces. That kind of loyalty takes years to build.

Location and getting around — Room@Vipa sits in Vibhavadi Rangsit Soi 44, roughly 100 metres off the main Vibhavadi Rangsit Road. Bang Khen station on the SRT Dark Red Line is approximately 750 metres away — a 10-minute walk — which connects directly to Don Mueang Airport and Bang Sue Grand Station (the central interchange). MRT Ratchayothin (Blue Line) is around 2.78 km away, requiring a motorbike taxi or Grab. BTS Green Line stations at Kasetsart University or Ratchayothin are roughly 3 km. A 7-Eleven is immediately next to the hotel, and the surrounding neighbourhood offers student-priced food stalls and local restaurants within easy walking distance.

"I stayed here first for work in the Kaset area and liked it so much I kept coming back. The staff are genuinely warm, the rooms are consistently clean, and the price is excellent for Bangkok. It feels more like a home-stay than a hotel."

Rooms and facilities — Room@Vipa offers several room configurations to suit different group sizes: Single Room with Shared Bathroom at the budget end, through to Twin, Double, Triple and Quadruple rooms with private en-suite bathrooms. All rooms include air conditioning, complimentary bottled water, slippers, and an LED TV. Free Wi-Fi is available in common areas. A shared pantry on the 3rd floor is available to all guests, equipped with a medium-size refrigerator, microwave, toaster and basic kitchen utensils — handy for warming up food from the 7-Eleven next door or cooking light meals. The building has an elevator, an advantage over many guesthouses at this price point.

What real guests say — Compiled from Trip.com (89 reviews, score 8.7/10: Location 9.2, Service 8.8, Cleanliness 8.7, Amenities 8.3) and TripAdvisor (rated #215 of 837 B&Bs in Bangkok). Consistent praise: "staff are very kind and helpful," rooms clean every stay, location convenient near transit and 7-Eleven, excellent value for money, and a warm atmosphere that keeps guests returning. Honest caveats from reviews: beds and pillows in some rooms are firm, with a few guests waking with neck stiffness; some rooms have minimal furniture (bed and recliner, no desk); and the soi address can be tricky to find by taxi or Grab on a first visit.

The Kaset-Vibhavadi neighbourhood — This is not a shopping or nightlife district. Its character is shaped by Kasetsart University Bangkhen (Thailand's major agricultural university), which brings a calm, campus-adjacent energy. Or Tor Kor Market is a short ride away for premium produce and local food. Ngam Wong Wan Road offers a mix of local restaurants, small shops and everyday conveniences. For travellers who need to connect to Don Mueang Airport or who have business at Kasetsart University or government offices in the northern Bangkok corridor, Room@Vipa makes the logistics straightforward at a price that is hard to match.

Pricing and value — Single rooms with shared bathroom start from approximately ฿550–650/night in regular periods. Twin/Double rooms with private bathroom run ฿750–900, rising to around ฿1,200 during long weekends or peak periods. For Bangkok accommodation offering cleanliness, an elevator, free parking, attentive staff, and a walking connection to train transit at this price level — the value proposition is real. The trade-off is clear: no pool, no gym, no breakfast included. If you need all of those, look elsewhere. But if you want a clean, characterful, affordable base in northern Bangkok with staff who genuinely care, Room@Vipa delivers.

honestSummary: Room@Vipa does the essentials consistently well: clean rooms, genuine service, an elevator, free parking, and a location walkable to train transit. The loyalty of its repeat guests — some returning a dozen times — says more than any star rating. Honest caveats: beds can be firm, some rooms lack a desk, and the soi address requires sharing a pin with your driver. But for the price and what you get, this is one of the harder places to beat in northern Bangkok.
honestChecks: If you need a work desk for remote work or business travel — some Room@Vipa rooms only have a bed and recliner with no dedicated desk. Specify your need when booking or contact the hotel in advance to confirm the room configuration.

If you are a light sleeper or prone to neck and back pain — reviews flag that pillows and mattresses in some rooms are on the firm side. Ask front desk about a softer pillow option; staff are generally eager to help where they can.

If it is your first time in this area — Vibhavadi Rangsit Soi 44 runs deep into the neighbourhood and signage isn't prominent from the main road. Share your pin location via Line with the hotel before you depart; they respond quickly and can guide your driver.

tips.title: Share Your Pin on Line Before Arriving
tips.body: Vibhavadi Soi 44 runs deep into the block and signage isn't obvious from the road. The hotel responds quickly on Line and Facebook Messenger — share your Google Maps pin before you leave and they'll help guide your driver.

tips.title: Take the Train to Don Mueang Airport
tips.body: Bang Khen SRT Red Line station is a 10-minute walk from the hotel. A direct train to Don Mueang Airport saves considerable Grab fare, especially during rush-hour traffic on the expressway.

tips.title: Local Food is Cheap and Plentiful
tips.body: The Kaset-Vibhavadi neighbourhood has rice boxes, noodles, and local eateries within short walking distance, priced at ฿50–80 per meal. No breakfast included — but the area makes it easy to sort yourself out quickly.

tips.title: Ask for a Softer Pillow If Needed
tips.body: Some rooms have firm beds and pillows. Staff are consistently described as warm and accommodating — ask at front desk about alternative pillows or a mattress topper before bed, not after a bad night's sleep.

faq.q: Where is Room@Vipa and how do I get there?
faq.a: Room@Vipa is at 71/14 Vibhavadi Rangsit Soi 44, Lat Yao, Chatuchak, Bangkok 10900. The easiest public transit option is Bang Khen station on the SRT Dark Red Line, approximately 750 metres away (about 10 minutes on foot). From there, direct trains run to Don Mueang Airport and Bang Sue Grand Station, where you can connect to BTS, MRT and other lines. By Grab or taxi from Suvarnabhumi Airport, allow 45–60 min depending on traffic.

faq.q: What does Room@Vipa cost per night?
faq.a: Prices start from approximately ฿550–650/night for a Single Room with shared bathroom. Twin or Double rooms with private bathroom start around ฿750–900. Rates rise during long weekends and major events in the Kaset area. Compare Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com before booking — prices often differ between platforms.

faq.q: Is Room@Vipa good for travellers connecting through Don Mueang Airport?
faq.a: Yes — this is one of Room@Vipa's strongest use cases. Bang Khen SRT Red Line station (about 750 m walk) connects directly to Don Mueang Airport in a short ride. For early morning departures or late arrivals, it is a significantly more affordable base than staying near the airport itself, and the area is quieter.

Breakfast is not included in the room rate. However, a 7-Eleven is immediately next to the hotel, and the neighbourhood has plenty of local food options for ฿50–80 per meal. Free parking is available for guests with a car — useful if you're road-tripping into Bangkok from the northern provinces.

faq.q: Who is Room@Vipa best suited for?
faq.a: Room@Vipa works best for travellers with business in the Kaset-Vibhavadi corridor, parents visiting students at Kasetsart University, and anyone flying through Don Mueang Airport who wants a clean, affordable base. Its repeat-guest community also suggests it appeals strongly to solo travellers and couples who value character and service over amenities.
